title: CareLine Service Plans Agreement — Visits and Visit Charges
content:
**Section: visits and visit charges under CareLine Service Plans.**

**1. Tune-ups.** Tune-up visits are included up to the plan's count per plan year, cover the plan's tune-up scope, and do not carry over; a tune-up beyond the count is billed as a repair visit. The tune-ups used in a plan year are the annual tune-up visits of that plan year whose outcome is completed.

**2. Response and trip fee.** A repair or glass visit is offered within the plan's response window and carries one trip fee per visit however many openings are worked on, except that the plan's free trips per plan year carry none. The free trips used in a plan year are that plan year's repair visits, glass replacement visits and emergency board-up visits, after the waiting period, whose outcome was not a customer no-show and which carried no trip fee charge on the same date.

**3. Labor.** Labor is billed at the plan's hourly rate for the billable hours, which are the hours on site with the minimum applied and any time beyond it rounded up to the billing increment.

**4. Parts.** Parts carry the plan's discount off the published parts price.

**5. Glass and components.** Glass replacement outside warranty is billed at the plan's flat charge per sealed unit, weatherstripping and rescreening per opening or screen, and caulk resealing per opening.

**6. Waiting period.** Plan repair benefits (free trips, the parts discount, and included weatherstripping and rescreening) apply only after the waiting period counted from the enrolled date; before it the On-Call rates apply to repairs. Calendar days are counted from the day after the enrolled date, and benefits begin on the day after the last waiting day.

**7. Other makers.** Parts are not supplied for windows or doors of other makers, so only labor is offered on them.

The count of tune-ups and their scope, the response window, the trip fee, the free trips, the hourly rate, the minimum and the billing increment, the parts discount, the per-unit, per-opening and per-screen charges and the waiting period are the figures the product schedules set for the plan's tier.

### Section 3 in figures (hypothetical rate of 100.00 per hour, minimum 1.0 hour, increment 0.5 hour)

| Hours on site | Billable hours | Labor |
|---|---|---|
| 0.6 | 1.0, the minimum | 100.00 |
| 1.0 | 1.0 | 100.00 |
| 1.2 | 1.5, the time beyond the minimum rounded up to the increment | 150.00 |
| 2.0 | 2.0 | 200.00 |

### Section 6 on the calendar (hypothetical enrolled date 1 March 2026, waiting period of 30 calendar days)

- The first waiting day is 2 March 2026; the last waiting day is 31 March 2026.
- A repair on 31 March 2026 falls inside the waiting period: no free trip, no parts discount and no included weatherstripping or rescreening; the On-Call rates apply to the repair.
- A repair on 1 April 2026 falls on the day benefits begin: the plan repair benefits apply.
- A tune-up is not a plan repair benefit, so the waiting period does not affect it.

### Section 2, the trip fee per visit (hypothetical visits after the waiting period)

| Visit | Trip fee |
|---|---|
| One repair visit, four openings worked on, no free trip left in the plan year | One trip fee |
| One repair visit, one opening worked on, a free trip left in the plan year | None; the visit uses a free trip |
| Two repair visits on two different dates, no free trip left | One trip fee on each visit |

### Section 1, the tune-up count (hypothetical plan with one tune-up per plan year)

The first completed tune-up of the plan year is included. A second tune-up in the same plan year is beyond the count and is billed as a repair visit. An unused tune-up does not pass into the next plan year.
